# Checklist: ux
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 003-paginas-publicas | Date: 2026-09-09 -->

Requirement *quality* checks for the experience: whether the spec says enough about
accessibility, responsiveness, feedback and error states for someone to build them and someone
else to disagree. Not implementation tests — `apps/web/tests/public/` holds those.

Written after the implementation merged, so each row is adjudicated with the artefact that
answers it. Every `[ ]` carries an **OPEN** rationale naming what is still true.

| ID | Check | Dimension | FR/US Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| CHK042 | Does the spec fix the three design targets by name, so "responsive" cannot be satisfied at a fourth width nobody designed?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — 390 / 834 / 1440, the same `--bp-*` tokens feature 001 declared, read out of the token layer by the suite rather than retyped. | [responsiveness] | FR-021 | [x] |
| CHK043 | Does it say what *changes* between those widths per page, or only that each page must render at all?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN.** FR-021 says "renders at 390 / 834 / 1440 with the shell behaviour feature 001 decided" and stops. Per page, nothing states which layout switches where — so `/aulas` and `/calendario` shipping no rule at 834 is neither correct nor incorrect against the spec, only undescribed. The suite now refuses a media rule that resolves to no change, which is a floor, not the missing statement. | [responsiveness] | FR-021, SC-010 | [ ] |
| CHK044 | Is the touch-target rule bound to an element set, so a control added later is covered?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN** — same gap as CHK022. 44×44 is given; which elements must meet it is not. | [accessibility] | FR-022 | [ ] |
| CHK045 | Does the focus requirement say what the ring must look like, or only that focus is "visible"?<br>**Adjudicated:** the page specs fix 2px and the pages fix the colour per surface. It was not enough: the accent scored 1.00:1 on the pink CTA, 1.13:1 on the teal band and 1.62:1 in `EmptyState`, all shipped, because "visible" was never given a ratio. WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 is now asserted per region — by the test, not by the requirement. | [accessibility] | FR-023, SC-009 | [ ] |
| CHK046 | Is the contrast rule for the two light pages expressed as a ratio a machine can check?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN** — see CHK031. "Never pink for small text on white" has no threshold and no size boundary. | [accessibility] | FR-028 | [ ] |
| CHK047 | Does every listing state its empty state *and* the action that clears it, rather than only the message?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — FR-017 names the clearing action, and `EmptyState` makes it an `href` rather than a handler, so it works with no JavaScript. | [error-states] | FR-017, US2 | [x] |
| CHK048 | Does every listing state its error state *and* a retry that preserves what the visitor had typed?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, and the retry target is specified as the URL that failed, filter included — a retry that silently dropped the filter would report success for a different page. | [error-states] | FR-018, US1 | [x] |
| CHK049 | Is the empty state distinguished from the error state, so "no results" is not reported as a fault?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — two variants with different ornaments, and `role="alert"` on the error one only, so a screen-reader user is not trained to ignore it. | [feedback] | FR-017, FR-018 | [x] |
| CHK050 | Is the loading state specified concretely enough to build?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN, and unbuilt** — see CHK019. The wording is fine; there is no `loading.tsx` in the tree and no task owned FR-019. A visitor on a slow connection currently gets nothing between navigation and content. | [feedback] | FR-019 | [ ] |
| CHK051 | When an action needs an account, does the spec fix the microcopy rather than leaving it to the implementer?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — US7 quotes it: "Crie sua conta para curtir e evoluir como maker". | [feedback] | FR-015, US7 | [x] |
| CHK052 | Is that invitation actually reachable — is there a control that opens it?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN, owned by 004 (CLR-010).** No. See CHK041: the heart renders its count and nothing else, `CardProjeto` waits for a `curtir` island no page supplies, and no task in `tasks.md` owned it. The microcopy CHK051 praises appears nowhere in the product. | [feedback] | FR-015, US7 | [ ] |
| CHK053 | Does the spec say what a visitor sees where signed-in affordances would be — absence, or a disabled control?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, and it argues the choice: publish CTAs do not render, because "a disabled button they can never use is noise". | [feedback] | FR-016, US7 | [x] |
| CHK054 | Is the 3D preview's failure path specified as something the visitor is told, not only as a fallback?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — US6's error clause has two verbs, "falls back to the thumbnail **and reports the failure in place**". Only the first shipped; the report was added in run 8's repair, which is what re-reading this clause caught. | [error-states] | FR-014, US6 | [x] |
| CHK055 | Does the spec distinguish "no preview exists" from "the preview failed", so the visitor is not told of a fault that did not happen?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — US6 separates its Edge from its Error, and the component reports only on the Error branch. | [error-states] | FR-014, US6 | [x] |
| CHK056 | Is keyboard reachability stated for the card as a whole, given the card carries several targets?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN.** FR-023 says "cards are reachable by Tab and activated by Enter", but a card holds a title link, a heart and an arrow. Which of them is *the* card is never said, so tab order within a card is unspecified — the suite asserts no target is removed from the order, which is weaker. | [accessibility] | FR-023 | [ ] |
| CHK057 | Does the spec state the language of the interface, so copy cannot drift between pages?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, by the constitution's Principle 4 — labels and content in PT-BR, code in English — and every page spec is written in PT-BR. | [clarity] | Constitution P4 | [x] |
